column1:
Incorporating the November 2017 Beige Book into the December 13 FOMC statement assessment slightly strengthens the constructive macro tone. District reports described modest-to-moderate growth with tight labor markets and notable wage gains for professional, technical, and production roles, which aligns with the Committee’s view of a “strong” labor market and supports eventual firming toward the 2% inflation goal. Consumer spending was steady, with an upbeat outlook for holiday sales, though autos were softer. Hurricane-related rebuilding raised demand and construction-material costs, adding some cost-push pressure. Commercial real estate conditions were mixed.

Set against this backdrop, the Committee’s “gradual” path and ongoing balance-sheet normalization remain appropriate. However, the SLOOS indications of tighter consumer credit terms and softer loan demand act as a counterweight, suggesting a measured tightening trajectory despite the firmer wage backdrop and holiday-spending tailwinds.

Net effect: The Beige Book modestly upgrades the near-term demand and wage/inflation impulse versus SLOOS alone, keeping the balance of risks roughly even but nudging sentiment modestly higher.
